content.title: The Lost Kite
content.passage: On Sunday morning, Rohan and his sister Pinky went up to the terrace with a bright yellow kite. The wind was strong, and the kite rose high above the water tanks. Suddenly the string snapped. The kite drifted over the neighbour's mango tree and landed on the roof of the old bakery. Pinky laughed and said, "Now the baker has a new flag!" Rohan was sad at first, but then he smiled. They went downstairs and asked their grandfather to help them make a new kite.

passage.title: Moti
passage.text: Moti is a brown street dog who lives near Gupta Uncle's tea stall. Every morning, before the stall opens, Moti sits beside the bench and waits. When Gupta Uncle arrives, he gives Moti a biscuit and a bowl of water. In return, Moti barks loudly whenever a stranger comes near the stall at night. Last winter, Moti barked for a long time at midnight. Gupta Uncle's neighbour came out and found that the stall's gas cylinder was leaking. The next day, the whole lane bought Moti a warm blanket.

questions.prompt: What does Gupta Uncle give Moti every morning?

options.text: A biscuit and a bowl of water

questions.prompt: What did the neighbour find at midnight?
Why did the lane buy Moti a blanket?

options.text: To thank Moti for warning them about danger
Because Moti was new in the lane

questions.prompt: How would you describe Moti and Gupta Uncle?

options.text: Gupta Uncle wants Moti to leave

passage.title: Asha's Bicycle
passage.text: Asha saved her pocket money for eight months to buy a second-hand bicycle. It had a rusty bell and a torn seat, but its wheels were strong. Her brother laughed and said it looked older than their grandfather. Asha did not reply. Every Sunday she cleaned one part of the bicycle: first the chain, then the bell, then the seat, which she covered with an old cushion cover. After two months, her brother asked if he could borrow it to go to the market. Asha smiled and handed him the key to the lock.

lesson.title: Meet the Glimmers
sections: Glimmers are small imaginary animals that live near rivers.
A Glimmer always has exactly three legs and a striped tail.
Glimmers change colour: they turn blue when they are happy and grey when they are hungry.
A Glimmer eats only moon-berries, which grow only at night.
Baby Glimmers have plain tails. The stripes appear when they turn one year old.
When a Glimmer sees its own reflection, it hums.

recap.text: Remember: three legs, striped tail (plain for babies), blue = happy, grey = hungry, eats only moon-berries that grow at night, hums at its reflection.
